clue.text: Sweet little thing and a real sucker

definitions.text: little thing and a real sucker

explanation.definitionFit: A jelly baby is a British gum sweet shaped like a tiny infant; the second reading describes it as a small thing that is sucked, like an infant.

clue.text: Use a manoeuvre to get me up first

indicators.note: first tells us the turned piece comes ahead of the other one
in a down clue, up means the word me is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a ploy is a cunning manoeuvre or tactic

explanation.surface: Someone is told to use a clever stratagem to get themselves promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses a piece, and 'first' places it at the front of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone or something to work is a synonym of making use of them.

clue.text: Lavish as becomes a member of the Upper House

definitions.text: as becomes a member of the Upper House

explanation.walkthrough: The Upper House is the House of Lords, Britain's second parliamentary chamber, whose members are peers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish means grand or magnificent in style; the second sense is behaving like a peer of the realm in the House of Lords.

clue.text: Eating place for way out writer

indicators.note: the writer sits out, on the outside, with the way tucked within

parts.note: a biro is a ballpoint pen
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a restaurant suited to an eccentric author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way out' looks like 'eccentric', describing the writer; instead it means the street sits within the pen. Biro is the British everyday word for a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant, a kind of eating place.

clue.text: Corroborate in joining what could be a disorderly retreat

parts.note: could be supplies the verb be
a rout is a disorderly retreat after defeat

explanation.surface: Someone joining a retreat that might turn chaotic finds it confirms something.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'what could be a disorderly retreat' as BE A ROUT, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear out a claim is to confirm or support it, the same as corroborating it.

clue.text: Over-nice police officer cut down by a penalty

parts.note: a superintendent, shortened, is a super
a fine is a monetary penalty

explanation.surface: A fussy policeman is brought low by a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' is not a deletion of the answer's letters: it shortens superintendent to its familiar form SUPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Superfine can mean excessively refined or fastidious, which is what over-nice means.

clue.text: A capital they changed takes the biscuit

parts.note: Bern is the Swiss capital

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in a capital who changed things does something outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges THEY into ETHY. An Abernethy is a hard Scottish biscuit flavoured with caraway; 'takes the biscuit' is a British idiom for being outrageous.
explanation.definitionFit: An Abernethy is a type of plain caraway biscuit.

clue.text: Ladykiller upset by red bauble

indicators.note: upset means the letters of red bauble are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A womaniser is annoyed by a red Christmas decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladykiller' suggests a charming womaniser, but here it is literal: Bluebeard of folklore murdered his wives.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebeard is the folk-tale figure who killed a series of wives.

clue.text: Songbird repeatedly on target one hears

indicators.note: repeatedly says the sounded piece is given twice
one hears means the word for the target is taken by its sound

parts.note: the bull is the centre of a target

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher keeps hearing a songbird score bullseyes.
explanation.walkthrough: BULL said aloud gives BUL, and 'repeatedly' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulbul is a tropical Asian and African songbird, celebrated in Persian poetry.

clue.text: Racing model to reveal the mark of an injury

parts.note: to sport something is to show it off or display it
a scar is the mark left by an injury

explanation.surface: A model in a race shows the scar from an accident.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports car is a fast car built for performance, the kind of model used in racing.

clue.text: Order at the start of last month on Mrs Ruff

parts.note: the opening letters of December, the last month, give its abbreviation
the female ruff, a wading bird, is called a ree or reeve

explanation.surface: An instruction issued at the beginning of December to a woman called Mrs Ruff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mrs Ruff' looks like a person's name; it is the female of the ruff, a sandpiper, called a REE.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree is an official order or edict.

clue.text: Infallible evidence of stupidity

explanation.definitionFit: Infallible means unable to go wrong, as a design is that cannot be misused; read as two words, the answer is proof that someone is a fool.

clue.text: A letter to entertain is wasted.

parts.note: ef is the spelt-out name of the letter F
to fete someone is to entertain or honour them lavishly

explanation.surface: A letter of invitation to a party has gone to waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete means feeble and exhausted, worn out, much as wasted means weakened.

clue.text: Bob once worked on the logs-then dropped off

parts.note: a bob was a pre-decimal shilling, abbreviated S
to lumber is to fell and cut timber

explanation.surface: A man named Bob once worked as a logger and then fell asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name; it is old British slang for a shilling, written S. 'Dropped off' means fell asleep, with a nod to 'sleeping like a log'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slumbered means slept, and to drop off is to fall asleep.

clue.text: Everyone pass? That evens things up

definitions.note: a phrase describing a level state; the answer is the adjective for it

parts.note: all means everyone
a square pass in football or hockey is one played across the field

explanation.surface: A teacher announces that everyone passed, so the results are level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' suggests an exam result; it is the sporting square pass, played sideways across the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: All square means level, with the scores equal, so things have been evened up.

clue.text: Incredible story taking one year flat to translate

indicators.note: translate here means to convert the letters into a new arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A translator spends a whole year rendering an unbelievable tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to translate' rearranges I (one) with YEAR and FLAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy tale can mean a far-fetched, unbelievable story, an incredible one.

clue.text: … being a letter a Greek goddess returns

indicators.note: returns means the goddess's name is read backwards

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A Greek goddess returning with a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the previous one, but it reads on its own: ATE backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Look up and down

indicators.note: the word reads the same whether taken up or down the grid

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An instruction to glance upwards and then downwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up and down' sounds like a direction to look all around; it says the three letters read the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it.

clue.text: Disposed to a quiet time

parts.note: P, from piano, is the musical mark for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone is inclined to spend a peaceful while.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt to do something means inclined or likely to, so disposed to it.

clue.text: A melody to compose

parts.note: compose here means to calm or settle, so this is a tune for soothing someone, a child to sleep

explanation.walkthrough: 'compose' looks like writing music; it means to calm.
explanation.definitionFit: A lullaby is a gentle song sung to calm a child to sleep.

clue.text: He makes a hit as a cattleman

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who throws a blow is a puncher; in the US, a cowhand who drives cattle is a cowpuncher, shortened to puncher.

clue.text: Chew 17 across

indicators.note: chewing churns things around, so the letters of the other answer are mixed up

parts.note: the answer to the clue numbered 17 across is the Greek letter

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay: chewing the three letters of the Greek letter rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: To chew food is to consume it, so the clue's action is a synonym of eating.

clue.text: I've twisted in pain to win

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the word for pain

parts.note: an ache is a dull pain

indicators.note: twisted means the letters of I've are wrung into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has wrenched themselves, suffering in order to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' looks like a description of the sufferer's body; it is the anagram signal, and 'in' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve something is to attain or gain it, as you win a prize.

clue.text: Call for a solo effort-and no tricks

definitions.text: Call for a solo effort-and no tricks

parts.words: Call for a solo effort-and no tricks
parts.note: in the card game solo whist, a player can bid to win no tricks at all, playing alone

explanation.walkthrough: 'no tricks' sounds like a promise of honesty; in solo whist it is the bid itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Misère is the bid in solo whist undertaking to lose every trick.

clue.text: Supposing the Eastern priest turns up at Italian resort

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: if means supposing
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

explanation.surface: Assuming the holy man from the East appears on the Italian coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' looks like 'arrives'; it reverses IF and LAMA together, giving AMAL then FI.
explanation.definitionFit: Amalfi is a seaside town on the Amalfi Coast south of Naples.

clue.text: Uncomplicated herbaceous plant

explanation.definitionFit: Simple means plain and straightforward; as a noun it is an old word for a medicinal herb.

clue.text: Of course it also means freedom of access

explanation.definitionFit: An entrée is a dish, a course of a meal; it is also the right to enter, admission.

clue.text: Stands up for ace players

explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to defend it; champions are also winners, the best players.

clue.text: Fairness in an acting trade union

explanation.definitionFit: Equity means justice and impartiality; Equity is also the British actors' trade union.

clue.text: Cut down a bit and collapsed

parts.note: to fell a tree is to cut it down
a part is a bit or piece

explanation.surface: A tree, felled and chopped up a little, finally crumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell apart is an idiom for collapsed or disintegrated.

clue.text: Enters the lists

parts.note: the phrase suggests a knight entering a jousting arena, but it means putting names on registers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Enters the lists' is an old idiom for joining a contest, from the lists, a medieval tournament ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to put names on a register, or sign up.

clue.text: Offal, indeed, brought to the home

annotationWithheld.why: Offal, indeed, brought to the home: the only parse puts LIVER in DEED, with the single word 'indeed' read as 'in deed', so it is both the container indicator and the DEED fodder
annotationWithheld.clue: Offal, indeed, brought to the home
